title: Cooling coffee: two models compared with residuals

stimulus.title: Temperature of a cup of coffee
stimulus.html:
A cup of coffee is left on a table in a room kept at 2222 degrees Celsius. Its temperature is measured every 55 minutes. Two models are proposed: a linear model LL, found by linear regression on the data, and the model EE given by E(t)=22+70(0.952)tE(t) = 22 + 70(0.952)^t, where tt is in minutes and both models give degrees Celsius.
Temperature of the coffee, in degrees Celsius, t minutes after it is poured
tt (minutes)05101520
Temperature (degrees Celsius)92.076.565.055.348.4

parts.label: A(i)
parts.prompt: Use linear regression on the data to find L(t)=mt+cL(t) = mt + c. Give mm and cc as decimal approximations.

rubric.point: <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>m</mi><mo>=</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>2.168</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">m = -2.168</annotation></semantics></math> and <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>c</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>89.120</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">c = 89.120</annotation></semantics></math> (correct to three decimal places; both needed)
accept: <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>L</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">L(t)</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>2.168000</mn><mi>t</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>89.120000</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= -2.168000t + 89.120000</annotation></semantics></math>
values truncated to three decimal places

parts.sample: Linear regression on the lists gives <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>m</mi><mo>=</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>2.168000</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">m = -2.168000</annotation></semantics></math> and <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>c</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>89.120000</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">c = 89.120000</annotation></semantics></math>, so <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>L</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">L(t)</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>2.168000</mn><mi>t</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>89.120000</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= -2.168000t + 89.120000</annotation></semantics></math>. Both values are stored.

parts.label: A(ii)
parts.prompt: A residual is the actual value minus the predicted value. Find the residual of LL and the residual of EE at t=10t = 10.

rubric.point: Residual of <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>L</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">L</annotation></semantics></math>: <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>2.440</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-2.440</annotation></semantics></math>; residual of <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>E</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">E</annotation></semantics></math>: <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>0.198</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.198</annotation></semantics></math> (both, as actual minus predicted)
accept: <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>65</mn><mo>−</mo><mi>L</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>10</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>2.440</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">65 - L(10) = -2.440</annotation></semantics></math> and <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>65</mn><mo>−</mo><mi>E</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>10</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>0.198</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">65 - E(10) = 0.198</annotation></semantics></math>
values truncated to three decimal places

parts.sample: <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>L</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>10</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>67.440000</mn><mo>.</mo><mo>.</mo><mo>.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">L(10) = 67.440000...</annotation></semantics></math>, so the residual of <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>L</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">L</annotation></semantics></math> is <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>65</mn><mo>−</mo><mi>L</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>10</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>2.440</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">65 - L(10) = -2.440</annotation></semantics></math>. <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>E</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>10</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">E(10)</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mn>22</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= 22</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">+</mo><mn>70</mn><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0.952</mn><msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mn>10</mn></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">+ 70(0.952)^{10}</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mn>64.802341</mn><mo>.</mo><mo>.</mo><mo>.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= 64.802341...</annotation></semantics></math>, so the residual of <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>E</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">E</annotation></semantics></math> is <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>65</mn><mo>−</mo><mi>E</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>10</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>0.198</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">65 - E(10) = 0.198</annotation></semantics></math>.

parts.label: B(i)
parts.prompt: The residuals of LL at t=0,5,10,15,20t = 0, 5, 10, 15, 20 are, in order, positive, negative, negative, negative, positive. The residuals of EE are all within 0.50.5 of 00 with no pattern. Which model is more appropriate for the data? Give a reason for your answer.

rubric.point: <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>E</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">E</annotation></semantics></math>, with a reason from the residuals: the residuals of <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>E</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">E</annotation></semantics></math> are small with no pattern, while those of <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>L</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">L</annotation></semantics></math> show a pattern (positive, negative, positive)
accept: "E: its residuals are close to 0 and patternless; L's residuals form a U, so the data curve away from the line"

parts.sample: <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>E</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">E</annotation></semantics></math> is more appropriate. Its residuals are small and show no pattern. The residuals of <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>L</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">L</annotation></semantics></math> go from positive to negative and back to positive, so the data bend upward away from the line, and a line has the wrong shape.

parts.label: B(ii)
parts.prompt: Use the model EE to predict the temperature of the coffee at t=30t = 30 minutes.
parts.sample: <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>E</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>30</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">E(30)</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mn>22</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>70</mn><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0.952</mn><msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mn>30</mn></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= 22 + 70(0.952)^{30}</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mn>38.003</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= 38.003</annotation></semantics></math> degrees Celsius.

parts.label: C
parts.prompt: (i) Use EE to find the time when the coffee is 4040 degrees Celsius. (ii) Explain why the model LL should not be used to predict the temperature an hour after the coffee is poured.

rubric.point: (i) <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>27.610</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t = 27.610</annotation></semantics></math> minutes, from solving <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>E</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>40</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">E(t) = 40</annotation></semantics></math> with a calculator
accept: an intersection of y = E(t) and y = 40 reported to three decimal places

rubric.point: (ii) <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>L</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">L</annotation></semantics></math> is decreasing without bound: it falls below the room temperature of <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>22</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">22</annotation></semantics></math> degrees after about <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>31.0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t = 31.0</annotation></semantics></math> minutes, which a cooling cup in a <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>22</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">22</annotation></semantics></math>-degree room cannot do
accept: "<math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>L</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>60</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>40.960</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">L(60) = -40.960</annotation></semantics></math>, below the room's <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>22</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">22</annotation></semantics></math> degrees"
a reason tied to the room temperature and the line decreasing forever

parts.sample: (i) Graph <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>E</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y = E(t)</annotation></semantics></math> and <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>40</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y = 40</annotation></semantics></math> and find the intersection: <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>27.610</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t = 27.610</annotation></semantics></math> minutes. (ii) <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>L</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">L</annotation></semantics></math> has a negative slope, so it keeps decreasing at the same rate. <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>L</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>60</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>40.960</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">L(60) = -40.960</annotation></semantics></math> degrees, below the room temperature of <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>22</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">22</annotation></semantics></math> degrees; in fact <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>L</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo><</mo><mn>22</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">L(t) < 22</annotation></semantics></math> for <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>></mo><mn>30.959</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t > 30.959</annotation></semantics></math>. Coffee in a <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>22</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">22</annotation></semantics></math>-degree room cools toward <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>22</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">22</annotation></semantics></math> degrees and does not drop below it, so <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>L</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">L</annotation></semantics></math> is not valid an hour after pouring. <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>E</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">E</annotation></semantics></math> approaches <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>22</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">22</annotation></semantics></math>, since <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><munder><mo movablelimits="false">lim</mo><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>→</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></mrow></munder><mi>E</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>22</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\lim_{t \to \infty} E(t) = 22</annotation></semantics></math>.
